title: ESA FIDUCIAL REFERENCE MEASUREMENT (FRM) ATLAS - EXPRO+

title: STUDY OF CELL-BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF AUTOPHAGY DEVELOPMENT UNDER MICROGRAVITY CONDITIONS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF TECHNOLOGIES FOR PRODUCING ESTABLISHED PLANT PRODUCTS ON SPACE PLATFORMS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Plants are expected to contribute to future exploration systems by providing food, biological resources and regenerative functions during long-duration missions. However, altered-gravity environments can affect plant growth, development, intracellular transport, stress signalling and resource allocation. Autophagy and programmed cell death are conserved cellular processes involved in the degradation and recycling of cellular components and in the regulation of plant development and stress adaptation. Their interaction with cytoskeletal organisation and metabolic regulation may therefore influence the capacity of plants to maintain stable growth and productivity under space-relevant conditions. The objective of the activity is to improve understanding of the cellular and molecular mechanisms that govern plant adaptation to altered-gravity conditions and to translate this knowledge into recommendations supporting reliable plant-based biological production on future space platforms.

title: EO4SLOVENIA - AN EO BASED SOLUTION FOR NATURAL HAZARDS AND WATER RESOURCES IN SLOVENIA - EXPRO+
description: Water Resources Management (WRM) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) are two thematic areas that are important in Slovenia. In 2025 a preparatory activity concerning the contribution of satellite data for different thematic areas has highlighted the needs of priorities of a group of nationally mandated stakeholders from both the WRM sector and the DRM sector. While the ESA Digital Twin Earth (ESA DTE) programme is looking at integrating Earth Observation (EO) satellite capabilities in future operational Digital Twins ecosystems, including the potential future evolution of DestinE and other operational DT initiatives in Europe, this activity is a precursor development under the FutureEO programme to prepare the ground for an EO based digital ecosystem and connect EO data, processingchains and modelling. This FutureEO activity aims to implement and demonstrate a preliminary Digital Twin Precursor to prefigure potential EO based Digital Twin developments. This ITT refers to implementing an EO-based Digital Twin precursor for the themes Water Resources Management and Disaster Risk Management for Slovenia identified through community consultation and considered to be mature enough to start a large activity. For both WRM and DRM themes, the project shall deliver end-to-end pre-operational solutions, fullyimplemented, conceptually and technically mature, scientifically validated, and fully tested by a representative set of early adopters.

title: AI ASSISTED SYSML V2 SPACE MODEL INTERACTION AND KNOWLEDGE REUSE - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and validate an AI-based assistant for interactive access, querying and assisted manipulation of SysML v2 space system models to reduce modelling effort and increase design quality.Description:Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) is an approach to manage the complexity of future space systems.Working effectively with large digital models is challenging; understanding structure and dependencies,reusing assets across projects, and extracting decision-relevant information is time-consuming andexpert-dependent.Limited and non-intuitive access to very large models slows MBSE adoption and reduces the return oninvestments, especially in early phases where it drives duplication, and late inconsistency discovery causeshigher design risk. SysML v2 introduces combined textual and graphical modelling with a standardised API for programmatic access, which lowers the access barrier. AI - and particularly Large Language Models (LLMs) - can help translate user intent into controlled, explainable interactions with these formal SysML v2 models, overcoming the barriers identified.This activity will develop an AI assistant that acts as an intermediate layer between users and formal modelsand operates exclusively via the SysML v2 textual notation and standard API. It will support (i) natural-language assistance for incremental model creation and modification, (ii) model querying and automated consistency checking, (iii) guided exploration of dependencies, (iv) identification and extraction of reusable model elements, and (v) structured summarization of model content for expert and non-expert stakeholders. The focus is on human assistance, incremental model generation and knowledge exploitation that helps system engineerswork with large system models - not on autonomous end-to-end model generation or mission-specifictoolchains.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of SysML v2 capabilities, APIs, and relevant AI techniques for model creation and interaction- Identification of representative use cases for querying, exploration, and reuse of SysML v2 models- Definition of a reference architecture ensuring controlled AI interaction via the SysML v2 API- Development of proof-of-concept AI components for model generation, querying and summarization- Validation of the approach on representative SysML v2 models, using the ESA MBSE methodology- Assessment of benefits, limitations, and roadmap towards higher TRL.The activity will result in validated concepts, software prototypes, and documented lessons learned, enablingfollow-on developments under GSTP or other programmes focusing on operational deployment.Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entitieswithin ESA Member States can access it and can provide update to the community of users.

title: PORTABLE SELF-CALIBRATED RYDBERG ELECTRIC FIELD PROBE FOR ANTENNA MEASUREMENTS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To design and realize a first European portable self-calibrated SI-traceable Rydberg atom-based Electric field probe.Description:Accurate measurement of electric fields is crucial for the development and operation of RF communicationsystems, particularly in space missions. Conventional antennas need fine calibration for high-integrity reception. The calibration is performed by placing uncalibrated antennas in a known EM (electromagnetic) environment that is measured via a well-calibrated antenna which creates a dependency. Whereas Rydberg based receivers allow precise measurements of RF signals which is directly related to Planck's constant and hence can self-calibrate by relying on SI (international system of units)-traceable atomic standards The activity aims to develop a portable, self-calibrated Rydberg atom based electric field probe.The probe is based on the interaction of RF-fields with Rydberg atoms, where alkali atoms are excited opticallyto Rydberg states and the applied RF-field alters the resonant state of the atoms. For this probe, the Rydbergatoms are placed in a glass vapor cell. The vapor cell acts like an RF-to-optical transducer, converting an RF Efield to an optical frequency response. The probe utilizes the concept of Electromagnetic Induced Transition (EIT), where the RF transition in the four-level atomic system causes a split of the transition spectrum for the pump laser. This splitting is measured and is directly proportional to the applied RF field amplitude. Therefore, by measuring this splitting, we get a direct measurement of the RF E-field strength. This technique could allow traceable measurements over a large frequency band including 1-500GHz. The new approach has the following benefits: 1) it will allow direct SI units linked RF E-field measurements, 2) It is self-calibrating due to atomic resonances, 3) it will provide RF field measurements independent of current techniques, 4) the probe will not perturb the field during the measurement, since no metal is present in the probe.This activity encompasses the following tasks:-Assessment of different Rydberg atom-based methods of detection of RF fields.- Requirement consolidation and performance assessment.- Detailed concept design with analysis of critical functions.- Development of the breadboard and verification in relevant environment.- Development of a technology roadmap for an EQM.
